claim: Differentiation of HT29-18N2 cells into mucin-secreting cells results in upregulation of KChIP3 mRNA levels by 3.3-fold compared to undifferentiated cells.
source: We re-tested mRNA levels of KChIP3 in differentiated HT29-18N2 goblet cells compared to undifferentiated cells. The data reveal a 3.3-fold increase in the mRNA levels of KChIP3 (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data presented in Figure 1A showing increased KChIP3 mRNA levels in differentiated versus undifferentiated cells.

claim: KChIP3-KD cells show an 80% reduction in KCNIP3 mRNA levels compared to control cells.
source: KChIP3-KD cells showed an 80% reduction in KCNIP3 mRNA levels, while levels of the other KChIP family members were unaffected (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data showing reduced KCNIP3 mRNA in KChIP3-KD cells.

claim: Depletion of KChIP3 leads to a 2.5-fold increase in baseline MUC5AC secretion.
source: Within 30 min, our results reveal a strong (2.5-fold) increase in baseline mucin secretion from KChIP3-depleted cells (Figure 1B)
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis of secreted MUC5AC from KChIP3-KD cells compared to control cells.

claim: KChIP3 depletion does not affect ATP-induced (stimulated) MUC5AC secretion.
source: but there was no effect on agonist (ATP)-induced (stimulated) MUC5AC secretion (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis showing no difference in ATP-stimulated secretion between KChIP3-KD and control cells.

claim: Overexpression of KChIP3 produces a 30% reduction in baseline MUC5AC secretion.
source: Conversely, overexpression of KChIP3 (KChIP3-GFP cells) produced a 30% reduction in baseline MUC5AC secretion (Figure 1D)
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis of secreted MUC5AC from KChIP3-GFP cells compared to control cells.

claim: Overexpression of KChIP3 does not affect ATP-dependent MUC5AC secretion.
source: without affecting ATP-dependent MUC5AC secretion (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis showing no difference in ATP-stimulated secretion between KChIP3-GFP and control cells.

claim: KChIP3-KD cells show a 5.7-fold increase in baseline MUC2 secretion compared to control cells.
source: KChIP3-KD cells showed a 5.7-fold increase in baseline secretion compared to control cells, while KChIP3-GFP cells presented a strong decrease (70.2% reduction compared to control cells) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis of secreted MUC2 from KChIP3-KD cells.

claim: KChIP3-GFP cells show a 70.2% reduction in baseline MUC2 secretion compared to control cells.
source: KChIP3-KD cells showed a 5.7-fold increase in baseline secretion compared to control cells, while KChIP3-GFP cells presented a strong decrease (70.2% reduction compared to control cells) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis of secreted MUC2 from KChIP3-GFP cells.

claim: KChIP3 depletion or overexpression does not affect total intracellular MUC5AC protein levels.
source: Total cell lysate from KChIP3-KD, KChIP3-GFP and control cells was dot blotted with anti-MUC5AC antibody and we did not observe any obvious difference in the total MUC5AC intracellular levels, compared to control HT29-18N2 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis of total cell lysates showing similar MUC5AC levels across conditions.

claim: KChIP3-KD cells contain significantly fewer MUC5AC granules than control cells (5.4 versus 13.7 particles/cell).
source: Our results reveal that KChIP3-KD cells contained significantly fewer granules than control cells: 5.4 MUC5AC-containing particles/cell versus 13.7 particles/cell (p=0.0239)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence images using 3D analysis software.

claim: KChIP3-GFP overexpressing cells show a dramatic accumulation of apical mucin granules with increased size compared to control cells (1.60 µm³ versus 0.90 µm³).
source: On the other hand, KChIP3-GFP overexpressing cells showed a dramatic accumulation of apical mucin granules, which was detected as an increase in the size of MUC5AC positive particles compared to control cells (1.60 µm3 in KChIP3-GFP cells compared to 0.90 µm3 in control cells, p=0.0038)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence images using 3D analysis software.

claim: HT29-18N2 cells exhibit spontaneous intracellular Ca²⁺ oscillations in the absence of stimulus (average of 30% of cells in 10 min).
source: Our data show that in the absence of stimulus, HT29-18N2 cells exhibit spontaneous intracellular Ca2+ oscillations (average of 30% of cells in 10 min) (Figure 2A, left panel)
evidence: The claim is supported by Fura-2AM calcium imaging data showing oscillations in unstimulated cells.

claim: Removal of extracellular Ca²⁺ increases the number of oscillating cells to 96% in 10 min.
source: 1) Removal of extracellular Ca2+ (solution with 0.5 mM EGTA), increased the number of oscillating cells (96% of cells in 10 min) (Figure 2A, central panel)
evidence: The claim is supported by Fura-2AM calcium imaging data in EGTA-treated cells.

claim: Inhibition of ryanodine receptors with 10 µM dandrolene reduces the number of Ca²⁺ oscillations to 13% of cells in 10 min.
source: and 2) inhibition of ryanodine receptors (RYRs) (treatment with 10 µM dandrolene (Zhao et al., 2001)) reduced the number of Ca2+ oscillations (13% of cells in 10 min) in either Ca2+-containing extracellular solutions (Figure 2A, right panel and quantification of oscillations in Figure 2B)
evidence: The claim is supported by Fura-2AM calcium imaging data in dandrolene-treated cells.

claim: Internal Ca²⁺ stores (principally the ER) are the source of Ca²⁺ oscillations in goblet cells.
source: These data implicate internal Ca2+ stores (principally the ER) as the source of Ca2+ oscillations in goblet cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the effects of EGTA and dandrolene on Ca²⁺ oscillations.

claim: Ryanodine receptors are involved in the generation and maintenance of Ca²⁺ oscillations in goblet cells.
source: Importantly, our data show that RYRs are involved in the generation and maintenance of these oscillations.
evidence: The claim is supported by the effect of dandrolene (RYR inhibitor) on reducing Ca²⁺ oscillations.

claim: Increasing Ca²⁺ oscillations by EGTA treatment increases baseline MUC5AC secretion by 60% compared to control.
source: Our results show that increased Ca2+ oscillations (EGTA treatment) correlate with increased baseline mucin secretion (60% higher than control)
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis of MUC5AC secretion in EGTA-treated cells.

claim: Reducing Ca²⁺ oscillations with 10 µM dandrolene reduces baseline MUC5AC secretion by 40%.
source: while fewer Ca2+ oscillations, in cells treated with 10 µM dandrolene, result in reduced baseline secretion (40% reduction) (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis of MUC5AC secretion in dandrolene-treated cells.

claim: Intracellular Ca²⁺ oscillations play an important role in baseline mucin secretion.
source: Altogether, these data suggest that intracellular Ca2+ oscillations play an important role in baseline mucin secretion.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the correlation between Ca²⁺ oscillation frequency and mucin secretion levels.

claim: Increasing Ca²⁺ oscillations by EGTA treatment increases MUC5AC secretion in control but not in KChIP3-KD cells.
source: Our results show that increasing Ca2+ oscillations by removing extracellular Ca2+ (EGTA solution) increased MUC5AC secretion in control but not in KChIP3-KD cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis comparing EGTA effects on control and KChIP3-KD cells.

claim: EGTA treatment abolishes the differences in mucin secretion between control and KChIP3-KD cells.
source: Furthermore, EGTA treatment abolished the differences in mucin secretion between control and KChIP3-KD cells (2.1 vs. 2.5 fold increase, respectively)
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis showing similar secretion levels in both cell types after EGTA treatment.

claim: Decreasing Ca²⁺ oscillations with dandrolene equally reduces baseline mucin secretion in both control and KChIP3-KD cells.
source: Additionally, decreasing the number of Ca2+ oscillations (dandrolene treatment) equally reduced baseline mucin secretion in both control and KChIP3-KD cells (Figure 2E)
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis showing similar reduction in secretion in both cell types after dandrolene treatment.

claim: KChIP3-MUT cells show a 37% decrease in baseline MUC5AC secretion compared to control cells under normal basal Ca²⁺ conditions.
source: Under normal basal Ca2+ conditions (1.2 mM CaCl2), differentiated KChIP3-MUT cells showed a similar reduction in baseline MUC5AC (Figure 2F) and MUC2 secretion (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B) as KChIP3-GFP cells (37% and 47% decrease compared to control, respectively) compared to control cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis of MUC5AC secretion from KChIP3-MUT cells.

claim: Increasing intracellular Ca²⁺ oscillations with EGTA induces a 47.6% increase in MUC5AC secretion in KChIP3-GFP cells.
source: While KChIP3-GFP cells showed increased secretion of MUC5AC identical to control cells (47.1% increase in control cells vs. 47.6% in KChIP3-GFP cells), KChIP3-MUT cells only showed an 11.1% increased secretion (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis of MUC5AC secretion from KChIP3-GFP cells treated with EGTA.

claim: Increasing intracellular Ca²⁺ oscillations with EGTA induces only an 11.1% increase in MUC5AC secretion in KChIP3-MUT cells.
source: While KChIP3-GFP cells showed increased secretion of MUC5AC identical to control cells (47.1% increase in control cells vs. 47.6% in KChIP3-GFP cells), KChIP3-MUT cells only showed an 11.1% increased secretion (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis of MUC5AC secretion from KChIP3-MUT cells treated with EGTA.

claim: Reducing intracellular Ca²⁺ oscillations with dandrolene markedly reduces MUC5AC secretion regardless of the form of KChIP3 overexpressed.
source: On the other hand, reducing intracellular Ca2+ oscillations with dandrolene treatment markedly reduced MUC5AC secretion regardless of the form of KChIP3 overexpressed (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis showing reduced secretion in all cell types after dandrolene treatment.

claim: KChIP3 has no role in the generation of spontaneous intracellular Ca²⁺ oscillations in HT29-18N2 goblet cells.
source: Thus, we conclude that KChIP3 has no role in the generation of spontaneous intracellular Ca2+ oscillations or ATP-mediated Ca2+ entry in HT29-18N2 goblet cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by Fura-2AM calcium imaging showing no difference in oscillation frequency between KChIP3-KD, KChIP3-GFP, and control cells.

claim: KChIP3 has no role in ATP-mediated Ca²⁺ entry in HT29-18N2 goblet cells.
source: Thus, we conclude that KChIP3 has no role in the generation of spontaneous intracellular Ca2+ oscillations or ATP-mediated Ca2+ entry in HT29-18N2 goblet cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by Fura-2AM calcium imaging showing no difference in ATP-induced Ca²⁺ response between KChIP3-KD, KChIP3-GFP, and control cells.

claim: There is no difference in basal Ca²⁺ levels between KChIP3-KD, KChIP3-GFP, and control cells.
source: Our results show no difference in basal Ca2+ levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D), ATP-dependent Ca2+ entry (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F), or in the number of cells exhibiting Ca2+ oscillations in KChIP3-KD or KChIP3-GFP cells compared to control cells (33% in KChIP3-KD, 37% in KChIP3-GFP, 30% in control cells) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by Fura-2AM calcium imaging data showing similar basal Ca²⁺ levels across cell types.

claim: The number of cells exhibiting Ca²⁺ oscillations is similar in KChIP3-KD (33%), KChIP3-GFP (37%), and control cells (30%).
source: Our results show no difference in basal Ca2+ levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D), ATP-dependent Ca2+ entry (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F), or in the number of cells exhibiting Ca2+ oscillations in KChIP3-KD or KChIP3-GFP cells compared to control cells (33% in KChIP3-KD, 37% in KChIP3-GFP, 30% in control cells) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of Fura-2AM calcium imaging data.

claim: Ca²⁺ oscillations generated in goblet cells are sensed by KChIP3 to control baseline mucin secretion.
source: Altogether, these results suggest that Ca2+ oscillations generated in goblet cells are sensed by KChIP3 to control baseline mucin secretion.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined data showing Ca²⁺ oscillations affect KChIP3 function but KChIP3 does not affect Ca²⁺ oscillations.

claim: KChIP3 in its Ca²⁺-free form acts as a repressor for baseline mucin secretion.
source: We further propose that KChIP3 in its Ca2+-free form acts as a repressor for baseline mucin secretion.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that KChIP3-MUT (which cannot bind Ca²⁺) shows reduced secretion and increased granule association.

claim: 10-15% of total MUC5AC granules detected by immunofluorescence contain KChIP3-GFP.
source: Our data reveal that 10 – 15% of total MUC5AC granules, detected by immunofluorescence (IF), contain KChIP3-GFP (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, upper panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence images.

claim: In KChIP3-GFP cells under basal conditions, 40.6% of KChIP3 signal colocalizes with MUC5AC.
source: Quantification of the images (using FIJI software, and described in materials and methods) revealed that in KChIP3-GFP cells under basal conditions, 40.6% of KChIP3 signal colocalized with MUC5AC (Average Manders' coefficient = 0.4061) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by colocalization analysis using Manders' coefficient.

claim: 59% of KChIP3-MUT signal colocalizes with MUC5AC under basal conditions.
source: In accordance with the functional data presented in the previous section, KChIP3-MUT showed very similar localization to KChIP3-GFP and even higher colocalization with MUC5AC granules (59% of KChIP3-MUT signal colocalizing with MUC5AC under basal conditions) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, lower panel; quantification in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by colocalization analysis using Manders' coefficient.

claim: KChIP3 associates with a pool of mucin granules in a Ca²⁺-free form.
source: These data suggests that KChIP3 associates with a pool of mucin granules in a Ca2+-free form.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the higher colocalization of KChIP3-MUT (which cannot bind Ca²⁺) with MUC5AC granules.

claim: The percentage of KChIP3 colocalizing with MUC5AC granules remains stable over time under normal conditions (41% at t=0 vs. 46% at t=30' for KChIP3-GFP).
source: Our data show that the percentage of KChIP3 colocalizing with MUC5AC granules remains stable over time (KChIP3-GFP: 41% at t = 0 vs. 46% at t = 30', Figure 3A left panel, KChIP3-MUT: 59% at t = 0 vs. 51% at t = 30', Figure 3B left panel) under normal conditions.
evidence: The claim is supported by colocalization analysis at different time points.

claim: Increasing Ca²⁺ oscillations by EGTA treatment for 30 min reduces the number of KChIP3-GFP positive granules.
source: Interestingly, increasing the number of the oscillations by EGTA treatment for 30 min at 37°C, reduced the number of KChIP3-GFP positive granules (Figure 3A, central panel) (quantified in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E as the volume of KChIP3 signal, 12 µm3 vs. 4.4 µm3, respectively)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of KChIP3-GFP volume in immunofluorescence images.

claim: Increasing Ca²⁺ oscillations by EGTA treatment reduces colocalization between KChIP3-GFP and MUC5AC (34% control vs. 19% EGTA treated cells).
source: and colocalization with MUC5AC (34% control vs. 19% EGTA treated cells)
evidence: The claim is supported by colocalization analysis comparing control and EGTA-treated conditions.

claim: EGTA treatment does not affect KChIP3-MUT localization to granules (52% in control vs. 54% in EGTA treated cells colocalization with MUC5AC).
source: but it did not have any effect on KChIP3-MUT localization to granules (Figure 3B central panel) (52% in control vs. 54% in EGTA treated cells colocalization with MUC5AC, Figure 3—figure supplement 1F)
evidence: The claim is supported by colocalization analysis showing no change in KChIP3-MUT localization after EGTA treatment.

claim: Reducing the number of Ca²⁺ peaks with dandrolene does not significantly affect the number of KChIP3 accumulations or colocalization to MUC5AC granules in KChIP3-GFP cells.
source: Finally, reducing the number of Ca2+ peaks did not significantly affect the number of KChIP3 accumulations or colocalization to MUC5AC granules in KChIP3-GFP (Figure 3A right panel, quantifications in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D and E)
evidence: The claim is supported by colocalization and volume analysis in dandrolene-treated cells.

claim: Intracellular Ca²⁺ oscillations regulate KChIP3 localization at MUC5AC granules.
source: In sum, our data show that intracellular Ca2+ oscillations regulate KChIP3 localization at MUC5AC granules
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that EGTA treatment reduces KChIP3-GFP localization to granules.

claim: Increase in Ca²⁺ oscillations reduces KChIP3 localization to MUC5AC granules.
source: Increase in Ca2+ oscillations reduces KChIP3 localization to MUC5AC granules
evidence: The claim is supported by colocalization analysis showing reduced KChIP3-GFP on granules after EGTA treatment.

claim: Impairing Ca²⁺ binding to KChIP3 results in more KChIP3-containing MUC5AC granules.
source: whereas impairing Ca2+ binding to KChIP3 results in more KChIP3-containing MUC5AC granules.
evidence: The claim is supported by the higher colocalization of KChIP3-MUT with MUC5AC granules and its insensitivity to EGTA treatment.

claim: KChIP3, encoded by the gene Kcnip3, is expressed in the colon of wild type mice.
source: KChIP3, encoded by the gene Kcnip3, is expressed in the colon of wild type (WT) mice and its deletion (Kcnip3-/- mice) does not affect the levels of the other members of the family (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data showing Kcnip3 expression in WT mouse colon.

claim: Deletion of Kcnip3 in mice does not affect the levels of the other KChIP family members.
source: KChIP3, encoded by the gene Kcnip3, is expressed in the colon of wild type (WT) mice and its deletion (Kcnip3-/- mice) does not affect the levels of the other members of the family (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data showing similar levels of other KChIP family members in WT and Kcnip3-/- mice.

claim: Kcnip3-/- mice exhibit decreased chronic neuropathic or inflammatory acute pain behaviours, without any major defects in locomotion, learning or memory.
source: Kcnip3-/- mice are reported to exhibit decreased chronic neuropathic or inflammatory acute pain behaviours, without any major defects in locomotion, learning or memory (Cheng et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Distal colon of Kcnip3-/- mice shows significantly increased mucus layer thickness compared to WT mice (77.0 µm versus 43.0 µm) as measured by PAS staining.
source: Impressively, distal colon of Kcnip3-/- mice revealed significantly increased levels of mucus layer compared to WT mice for both PAS (43.0 µm control vs. 77.0 µm Kcnip3-/-) (Figure 4A and B)
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis and quantification of PAS-stained colon sections.

claim: Distal colon of Kcnip3-/- mice shows significantly increased mucus layer thickness compared to WT mice (73.6 µm versus 40.5 µm) as measured by PAS-AB staining.
source: and PAS-AB (40.5 µm in WT mice vs. 73.6 µm in Kcnip3-/- mice) (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis and quantification of PAS-AB-stained colon sections.

claim: The increase in mucus layer was detected in the medial colon of four out of five Kcnip3-/- mice.
source: In addition, this increase in the mucus layer was also detected in the medial colon of four out of five Kcnip3-/- mice (average thickness, PAS: 31.6 µm WT mice vs. 50.3 µm Kcnip3-/- mice, NS; PAS-AB: 33.6 µm WT mice vs. 54.0 µm Kcnip3-/- mice, NS) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis of medial colon sections.

claim: The colonic mucus layer in Kcnip3-/- mice seems denser, suggesting that the viscoelastic properties of the gel-forming mucins are altered.
source: Additionally, the colonic mucus layer in Kcnip3-/- mice seems denser (Figure 4), suggesting that the viscoelastic properties of the gel-forming mucins are also altered.
evidence: The claim is based on visual observation of histological images and speculation about mucin properties.

claim: Mucins are encoded by 21 different genes in mammals.
source: Mucins, encoded by 21 different genes in mammals, are the major components of the mucus layer, which provides the first line of defense against pathogens and allergens to the lining of the respiratory, urinary, gastrointestinal and reproductive tracts (Boucher, 2007; Kesimer et al., 2013; Russo et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Mucins are the major components of the mucus layer, which provides the first line of defense against pathogens and allergens.
source: Mucins, encoded by 21 different genes in mammals, are the major components of the mucus layer, which provides the first line of defense against pathogens and allergens to the lining of the respiratory, urinary, gastrointestinal and reproductive tracts (Boucher, 2007; Kesimer et al., 2013; Russo et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Specialized epithelial goblet cells secrete gel-forming mucins (MUC2, MUC5AC, MUC5B and MUC6) that control the rheological properties of the mucus layer.
source: Specialized epithelial goblet cells secrete gel-forming mucins (MUC2, MUC5AC, MUC5B and MUC6) that control the rheological properties of the mucus layer (Davis and Dickey, 2008; Kreda et al., 2012; Thornton et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Mucins are synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) where they undergo core glycosylation and reach up to 500 kDa in apparent molecular weight.
source: Mucins are synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) where they undergo core glycosylation and reach up to 500 kDa in apparent molecular weight.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Fully assembled mucins are exported to the Golgi complex where, after extensive glycosylation, they reach sizes of up to 2.5 million daltons.
source: The fully assembled mucins are then exported to the Golgi complex where, after extensive glycosylation, they reach sizes of up to 2.5 million daltons (Sheehan et al., 2004; Thornton et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Heavily glycosylated mucins are packed into secretory granules that can be up to a micron in size and occupy almost 75% of the cytoplasmic volume.
source: These heavily glycosylated mucins are then packed into secretory granules that can be up to a micron in size and occupy almost 75% of the cytoplasmic volume (Curran and Cohn, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Mucin granules mature to produce highly condensed mucins and a subset of granules fuse with the plasma membrane by SNARE-mediated fusion.
source: The granules mature to produce highly condensed mucins and finally a subset of granules fuse with the plasma membrane by SNARE-mediated fusion (Adler et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: In the extracellular space, condensed mucins undergo a change in their organization to a gel-like form to compose a layer of mucus that coats the extracellular surface of the epithelium.
source: In the extracellular space, condensed mucins undergo a change in their organization to a gel-like form to compose a layer of mucus that coats the extracellular surface of the epithelium (Thornton et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Mucin granule exocytosis is a Ca²⁺-regulated process that can occur at basal level (Baseline Mucin Secretion, BMS) and by an exogenously supplied agonist dependent release (Stimulated Mucin Secretion, SMS).
source: Mucin granule exocytosis is a Ca2+-regulated process that can occur at basal level (Baseline Mucin Secretion, BMS) and by an exogenously supplied agonist dependent release (Stimulated Mucin Secretion, SMS) (Adler et al., 2013; Rossi et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Baseline mucin secretion could be the preponderant mode of goblet cell mucin release in healthy tissue, and may contribute predominately to mucus formation in allergic and infectious inflammation.
source: Importantly, baseline mucin secretion could be the preponderant mode of goblet cell mucin release in healthy tissue, and may contribute predominately to mucus formation in allergic and infectious inflammation (Zhu et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Synaptotagmin 2 (Syt2) has low affinity and high cooperativity for Ca²⁺ binding.
source: The Ca2+ binding properties of the well-characterized Synaptotagmin 2 (Syt2: low affinity and high cooperativity (Xu et al., 2007)) provide the high fidelity necessary for stimulated secretion.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Syt2 does not have a role in baseline mucin secretion.
source: Syt2, however, does not have a role in baseline mucin secretion (Tuvim et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: A genome-wide screen identified TRPM5, a Na⁺ channel that controls extracellular Ca²⁺ entry into cells, as a regulator of mucin secretion.
source: Our genome-wide screen identified new proteins that regulate mucin secretion, such as TRPM5, a Na+ channel that controls extracellular Ca2+ entry into cells (Mitrovic et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: KChIP3 is a high-affinity Ca²⁺-binding protein, also known as DREAM and Calsenilin.
source: Also identified in the pool of hits from this screen, was a high-affinity Ca2+-binding protein, KChIP3 (potassium voltage-gated channel interacting protein 3), also known as DREAM and Calsenilin (An et al., 2000; Buxbaum et al., 1998; Carrión et al., 1999), which is encoded by the gene KCNIP3.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: KChIP3 is a member of the neuronal Ca²⁺ sensor protein (NCS) family that codes a 29 kDa multifunctional Ca²⁺-binding protein.
source: KChIP3 is a member of the neuronal Ca2+ sensor protein (NCS) family that codes a 29 kDa multifunctional Ca2+-binding protein (Carrión et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: KChIP3 has three functional EF hands and can bind two Ca²⁺ ions with high affinity and another with lower affinity.
source: It has three functional EF hands and can bind two Ca2+ ions with high affinity and another with lower affinity (Lusin et al., 2008; Osawa et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The Ca²⁺ regime under which KChIP3 senses Ca²⁺ is at < 1 µM, which is an order of magnitude lower than the levels required to regulate stimulated secretion (estimated at 10 µM).
source: Curiously, the Ca2+ regime under which KChIP3 senses Ca2+, at < 1 µM, is an order of magnitude lower than the levels required to regulate stimulated secretion, which is estimated at 10 µM in the vicinity of the exocytic machinery in goblet cells (Rossi et al., 2004; Yu et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Baseline mucin secretion can release mucins in quantities that exceed several-fold the amounts released by the agonist-mediated process over a 24 hr period.
source: Recent studies suggest that baseline secretion can release mucins in quantities that exceed several-fold, the amounts released by the agonist-mediated process over a 24 hr period (Zhu et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Baseline mucin secretion in human bronchial epithelial cells and mouse trachea involves SNAP23 and Munc13-2, which also regulate stimulated secretion.
source: In a nutshell, all that is known at present about baseline mucin secretion in human bronchial epithelial cells and mouse trachea is the involvement of SNAP23 and Munc13-2, which also regulate stimulated secretion (Ren et al., 2015; Zhu et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Baseline mucin secretion is independent of Syt2 and sensitive to mechanical stress.
source: It is also known that baseline mucin secretion is independent of Syt2 and sensitive to mechanical stress (Zhu et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: KChIP3 is the high-affinity calcium sensor that controls baseline mucin secretion.
source: We propose KChIP3 as the high-affinity calcium sensor to control baseline mucin secretion.
evidence: The claim is the main conclusion of the study, supported by the experimental data presented.

claim: KChIP3 is a negative regulator of baseline mucin secretion.
source: KChIP3 according to our data is a negative regulator of baseline mucin secretion.
evidence: The claim is supported by the observation that KChIP3 depletion increases secretion while overexpression decreases it.

claim: Syt2 is the low-affinity calcium sensor that acts positively to regulate stimulated mucin secretion.
source: Syt2, on the other hand, is the low-affinity calcium sensor that acts positively to regulate stimulated mucin secretion (Tuvim et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Mature granules for baseline secretion are already docked at plasma membrane and ready to release their contents.
source: One possibility is that mature granules for baseline secretion are already docked at plasma membrane and ready to release their contents.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the mechanism of baseline secretion.

claim: KChIP3 may compete with a positive regulator, like synaptotagmins, to control baseline mucin secretion.
source: Another possibility that we cannot exclude is that KChIP3 competes with a positive regulator, like synaptotagmins, to control baseline mucin secretion.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the mechanism of KChIP3 function.

claim: The function of KChIP3 is conserved in mucin secreting goblet cells regardless of the tissue.
source: In addition, we propose that even though there are notable differences in the proposed mechanisms of mucin secretion between colonic and airway cells, the function of KChIP3 is conserved in mucin secreting goblet cells regardless of the tissue.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that KChIP3 regulates mucin secretion in colonic cells and the known similarities in mucin secretion mechanisms.

claim: Both stimulated and baseline secretion in the airways are affected by shear stress (airflow and mucus movements promoted by ciliated cells), but are independent of extracellular Ca²⁺.
source: For example, both stimulated and baseline secretion in the airways are affected by shear stress (airflow and mucus movements promoted by ciliated cells), but are independent of extracellular Ca2+ (Davis and Dickey, 2008; Tuvim et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In the intestine, there are two layers of mucus, an outer loose layer and an inner adherent layer of MUC2 (which is free of pathogens).
source: In the intestine, there are two layers of mucus, an outer loose layer and an inner adherent layer of MUC2 (which is free of pathogens) (Johansson et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Extracellular Ca²⁺ is required for stimulated secretion in the intestine.
source: and extracellular Ca2+ is required for stimulated secretion (Mitrovic et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Mucin secretion in both airways and the colon requires intracellular Ca²⁺.
source: Nevertheless, mucin secretion in both airways and the colon requires intracellular Ca2+.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about mucin secretion mechanisms.

claim: There exists a low affinity Ca²⁺ sensor for stimulated secretion and a high affinity Ca²⁺ sensor for baseline secretion regardless of the tissue type.
source: Altogether, this suggests the existence of a low affinity Ca2+ sensor for stimulated secretion and a high affinity Ca2+ sensor for baseline secretion regardless of the tissue type.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the data on KChIP3 and previous knowledge about Syt2.

claim: KChIP3 likely plays an important role in the physiology and pathophysiology of colon, the airways and consequently in mucin related pathologies such as asthma, cystic fibrosis and COPD.
source: KChIP3, as the high affinity Ca2+ sensor, therefore likely plays an important role in the physiology and pathophysiology of colon, the airways and consequently in mucin related pathologies such as asthma, cystic fibrosis and COPD.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the broader implications of the findings.

claim: In neurons, KChIP3 alters ER calcium content and RYR-mediated Ca²⁺-induced Ca²⁺ release (CICR) by direct interaction with RYR receptors.
source: In neurons, KChIP3 alters ER calcium content and RYR-mediated Ca2+-induced Ca2+ release (CICR) by direct interaction with RYR receptors (Grillo et al., 2018; Lilliehook et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: ER is in close proximity to mucin granules in goblet cells.
source: It is reported that ER is in close proximity to mucin granules in goblet cells (Tuvim et al., 2009)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: By directly interacting with RYR, the activity and location of KChIP3 is affected by an ER-based Ca²⁺ oscillations.
source: which presents the possibility that by directly interacting with RYR, the activity and location of KChIP3 is affected by an ER-based Ca2+ oscillations.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on the proximity of ER to granules and known KChIP3-RYR interactions.

claim: KChIP3 couples Ca²⁺ release from ER to baseline mucin secretion.
source: KChIP3 in this manner couples Ca2+ release from ER to baseline mucin secretion.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the data showing KChIP3 responds to Ca²⁺ oscillations originating from ER.

claim: Ca²⁺-bound KChIP3 is soluble and cytoplasmic.
source: Based on our findings, we suggest that Ca2+-bound KChIP3 is soluble and cytoplasmic
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that increased Ca²⁺ reduces KChIP3 association with granules.

claim: Under conditions where KChIP3 is Ca²⁺-bound, cells release more mucins from the secretory granules.
source: under these conditions the cells release more mucins from the secretory granules.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the correlation between increased Ca²⁺ oscillations, reduced granule-associated KChIP3, and increased secretion.

claim: Granule-bound KChIP3 inhibits events leading to SNARE-mediated fusion.
source: We suggest a parsimonious model, that granule-bound KChIP3 inhibits events leading to SNARE-mediated fusion.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the mechanism of KChIP3 function.

claim: Ca²⁺ oscillations generated in the proximity of mucin granules from the ER reach a certain threshold (provided by KChIP3's Ca²⁺ binding properties) to trigger baseline mucin secretion.
source: Altogether, we suggest that Ca2+ oscillations generated in the proximity of mucin granules from the ER, and not small increases in mean cytoplasmic calcium concentration, reach a certain threshold (provided by KChIP3's Ca2+ binding properties) to trigger baseline mucin secretion.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the data on Ca²⁺ oscillations, KChIP3 localization, and secretion.

claim: Binding of Ca²⁺ to KChIP3 changes its conformation thereby affecting its interaction to mucin granules.
source: We hypothesize that binding of Ca2+ to KChIP3 changes its conformation thereby affecting its interaction to mucin granules.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the molecular mechanism of KChIP3 function.

claim: KChIP3 bound to Ca²⁺ dissociates from DRE sites in its role as a transcriptional repressor.
source: This, we suggest, is analogous to KChIP3's association to DRE sites where it acts as a transcriptional repressor. In this scheme, KChIP3 bound to Ca2+ dissociates from DRE sites (Carrión et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Post biogenesis at the Golgi, mucin granules undergo maturation and are placed on path to fuse with the plasma membrane and release their contents.
source: Post biogenesis at the Golgi, mucin granules undergo maturation and are placed on path to fuse with the plasma membrane and release their contents.
evidence: The claim is part of the proposed model shown in Figure 5.

claim: Mature granules recruit KChIP3 (unbound to Ca²⁺) and this event stalls their fusion to the plasma membrane.
source: However, the mature granules recruit KChIP3 (unbound to Ca2+) and this event stalls their fusion to the plasma membrane.
evidence: The claim is part of the proposed model shown in Figure 5, based on the experimental data.

claim: KChIP3 recruitment acts as a brake to control the number of granules that can fuse with the plasma membrane.
source: KChIP3 recruitment thus acts as a brake to control the number of granules that can fuse with the plasma membrane.
evidence: The claim is part of the proposed model shown in Figure 5, based on the experimental data.

claim: In absence of intracellular Ca²⁺ oscillations, KChIP3 is bound to the granules preventing their secretion.
source: (A) In absence of intracellular Ca2+ oscillations, KChIP3 is bound to the granules preventing their secretion
evidence: The claim is part of the proposed model shown in Figure 5, based on the experimental data.

claim: Upon a rise in intracellular Ca²⁺ by RYR-induced Ca²⁺ oscillations, the KChIP3 on the granules binds Ca²⁺ and subsequently detaches thereby triggering their SNARE dependent fusion to the plasma membrane.
source: and (B) Upon a rise in intracellular Ca2+ by RYR-induced Ca2+ oscillations, the KChIP3 on the granules binds Ca2+ and subsequently detaches thereby triggering their SNARE dependent fusion to the plasma membrane.
evidence: The claim is part of the proposed model shown in Figure 5, based on the experimental data.

claim: Cells have evolved a mechanism by imposing the recruitment of empty KChIP3 to mucin granules to stall their progression leading to fusion with plasma membrane.
source: The cells have therefore evolved a mechanism by imposing the recruitment of empty KChIP3 to mucin granules to stall their progression leading to fusion with plasma membrane.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on the proposed model and experimental data.

claim: Specialized secretory cells based on the source of Ca²⁺ engage different Ca²⁺ binding proteins to release cargoes from the secretory granules.
source: In conclusion, specialized secretory cells based on the source of Ca2+ engage different Ca2+ binding proteins to release cargoes from the secretory granules.
evidence: The claim is a general conclusion based on the findings about KChIP3 and previous knowledge about Syt2.

claim: The agonist and extracellular Ca²⁺-dependent fast release employs low-affinity Ca²⁺ sensors like Syt2.
source: The agonist and extracellular Ca2+-dependent fast release employs low-affinity Ca2+ sensors like Syt2
evidence: The claim is based on previous knowledge about Syt2 function.

claim: The agonist-independent and intracellular Ca²⁺ oscillations exploit the function of a high-affinity Ca²⁺ sensor like KChIP3.
source: whereas the agonist-independent and intracellular Ca2+ oscillations exploit the function of a high-affinity Ca2+ sensor like KChIP3.
evidence: The claim is the main conclusion of the study, supported by the experimental data.
